title: Dirichlet p-adic L-functions, special values, and Eisenstein measures, Part II: Ray-class and automorphic interpolation
summary: Partial algebraic checkpoint for BSW evaluation: closure of unit invariance, weighted inversion, cancellation of representative changes, finite sums of evaluation functionals, and normalization along every prime above p. Nineteen declaration-sized nodes include twelve separately named API lemmas and twelve tests. The full-function algebraic dual is explicitly NOT identified with locally analytic distributions. Actual cohomological evaluation, continuity, norm relations, control and interpolation remain open. Approved RS-14 determines the title, base and supplier ownership. Three source findings are recorded for independent review; source-version collation is incomplete.

conventions.algebraicCore: G is a commutative group, L a field, w:G->L^times a multiplicative weight. V and M are L-modules. W_w f(z)=w(z)f(z^-1). D_u f(z)=w(u)f(u^-1 z). Linear duals of the full function space in these helper lemmas are algebraic duals, not a definition of the arithmetic distribution space.
conventions.charts: Use the forward fibre chart c_a(z)=a z and pullback psi_a(z)=phi(a z). If a'=a gamma u r and gamma,r die in the ray quotient, psi_a'(z)=psi_a(u z). The evaluation functional transforms contragrediently, nu'(f)=nu(D_(u^-1) f). This convention makes the two changes cancel. Source finding E1 records the mixed inverse convention in the checked preprint.
conventions.arithmetic: For arithmetic instantiation F is a number field, p rational prime, L/Q_p finite containing the relevant embeddings and eigenvalues, and the p-power modulus is divisible by EVERY prime above p. Global totally positive units enter through their actual topological closure; no Leopoldt assumption or prescribed quotient rank is inserted.
conventions.levels: P is the finite set of primes above p. A level is n:P->N; admissible levels have n(q)>=1 for every q. Eigenvalues alpha(q) are units in L, expressing the finite-slope nonzero condition. alpha_n=product_q alpha(q)^n(q). Uniformizers, the eigenclass, periods and refinements are fixed; conductor independence does not remove these choices.
conventions.separationOfClaims: Choice independence for the constructed functional is not uniqueness from interpolation. The latter requires a separately proved determining-family/growth theorem. No general-number-field admissibility uniqueness, family interpolation, ordinary projection or Selmer statement is asserted here.

declarations.provides: Existing algebraic dual M ->_L L. Inspected at the pin; used for the algebraic pairing core only, not as a locally analytic distribution carrier.
Existing transpose/precomposition on algebraic duals, inspected at the pin. It explains the contragredient representative action.
Existing subgroup closure, inspected at the pin. Do not rebuild the topological closure of the global unit image.
Equality of continuous maps into a Hausdorff space extends from a subset to its closure; actual statement and proof inspected at the pin.

Existing transition homomorphism between finite ray class groups for divisible moduli, inspected at the pin. The arithmetic inverse limit must reuse it rather than construct a competing finite carrier.

Existing compatibility of three finite-ray-class transition maps, inspected at the pin. This is an input to the still-unconstructed arithmetic inverse-limit topology, not evidence that that limit is already built.

nodes.title: Continuous unit invariance extends to the closure
nodes.statement: Let G be a topological group, E a subgroup, L a Hausdorff space and phi:G->L continuous. If phi(ez)=phi(z) for every e in E and z in G, the same equality holds for every e in the topological closure of E.
hypotheses: Multiplication on G is continuous; the codomain is Hausdorff. No compactness, rank computation, or Leopoldt conjecture is required.
proofSteps: Fix z. The maps e |-> phi(ez) and e |-> phi(z) are continuous and equal on E.
Apply the existing equality-on-closure theorem and then quantify over z.
acceptance: This proves closure invariance, not locally analytic descent or a quotient topology comparison.

sources.locator: Section 9.2.1 and the unit-invariance input to Definition 9.4, pp.30-31
sources.match: An explicit topological helper for the arithmetic unit quotient; the proof is a direct application of the cited baseline theorem, not an attribution of an extra analytic quotient theorem to the paper.

nodes.title: Weighted inversion on test functions
nodes.statement: For a commutative group G, field L and w:G->L^times, construct the L-linear endomorphism W_w of G->L given by W_w(f)(z)=w(z)f(z^-1).
hypotheses: No topology is asserted on the full function carrier. Arithmetic restriction to locally analytic test spaces requires the separate analytic worklist.
proofSteps: Define the indicated function pointwise. Distributivity and commutativity in L prove additivity and L-linearity.
Use the existing function-space module and LinearMap carrier, not a new distribution structure.
acceptance: Both the factor w(z) and the inverse argument are essential; the tests reject dropping either.

uses.how: Convert unit-invariant scalar test functions into weight-covariant coefficient functions before evaluation.

api.name: weightedTwist_translate
api.statement: W_w(f composed with multiplication by u)=D_u(W_w f); node twist-translation.

tests.name: twist_trivial_weight
tests.statement: For w=1, W_w f(z)=f(z^-1), for arbitrary f.

tests.name: twist_character_degree
tests.statement: For G=Q^times, w(z)=z^2 and f(z)=z^3, W_w f(2)=1/2, not 2 or 32.

tests.name: twist_constant_one
tests.statement: W_w applied to the constant function one is exactly the scalar-valued character w.

sources.match: The restriction of the source's twist to the unit group. Zero extension and locally analytic continuity are deliberately not silently supplied by this algebraic definition.

nodes.title: Weighted inversion evaluation
hypotheses: G commutative group, L field, w:G->L^times, f:G->L, z:G.
proofSteps: Unfold the linear-map evaluation once; expose the formula as a simplification lemma.
acceptance: The scalar is evaluated at z, not at z^-1.

sources.match: Pointwise API for the algebraic part of the source definition.

nodes.title: Weighted inversion is involutive
hypotheses: The weight takes values in units and is multiplicative.
proofSteps: At z the two scalar factors are w(z) and w(z^-1), whose product is one; inversion of the argument twice gives z.
Apply function extensionality.
acceptance: No assumption that w is trivial or quadratic is needed.

sources.match: Derived algebraic API; proved here from the definition, not claimed as a separately numbered source theorem.

nodes.title: Translation through weighted inversion
nodes.statement: For u in G, W_w(z |-> f(u z))(z)=w(u) W_w(f)(u^-1 z).
hypotheses: G commutative; notation D_u f(z)=w(u)f(u^-1 z).
proofSteps: Expand the right side as w(u)w(u^-1 z)f((u^-1 z)^-1).
Multiplicativity cancels the weights, and commutativity changes z^-1 u to u z^-1.
acceptance: The input translates by u, not u^-1; the opposite choice is tested in source finding E1.

sources.locator: Definitions 6.3-6.4 and proof of Proposition 9.6, pp.21 and 32
sources.match: The corrected algebraic calculation under the explicitly chosen forward-chart convention. Source E1 prevents importing the conflicting displayed convention verbatim.

nodes.title: Unit invariance becomes weight covariance
nodes.statement: If f(ez)=f(z) for all e in a subgroup E, then W_w(f)(ez)=w(e)W_w(f)(z) for e in E.
hypotheses: Weighted-inversion hypotheses; E is a subgroup and f is invariant under its translations.
proofSteps: The inverse of e belongs to E. Use its invariance at z^-1 and the inverse-of-product formula.
Split w(ez) by multiplicativity.
acceptance: The character factor is covariance, not invariance, unless w restricts trivially to E.

sources.locator: Definition 9.4 and its preceding invariance condition, p.31
sources.match: The algebraic reason the twisted test function is admitted by the coefficient evaluation.

nodes.title: Cancellation of a chart change in the pairing
nodes.statement: Let nu,nu' be L-linear functionals on G->L and u in G. If nu'(h)=nu(z |-> w(u^-1)h(u z)) for every h, then nu'(W_w(z |-> f(u z)))=nu(W_w f).
hypotheses: Weighted-inversion hypotheses. The given transformation is precomposition by D_(u^-1), not a blanket equality of the final pairings.
proofSteps: Move the stated contragredient action across the pairing.
Use twist-translation and cancel D_(u^-1) D_u pointwise; w(u^-1)w(u)=1.
acceptance: No arithmetic interpolation values or density assertion enter this calculation.

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 9.6, p.32, with source finding E1
sources.match: Extracts the precise algebraic cancellation. Actual cohomological transformation of nu is still an instantiation obligation.

nodes.title: Finite sum of twisted evaluations
nodes.statement: For a finite type Y, linear pullbacks T_y:V->(G->L) and nu_y in the algebraic dual of G->L, construct Eval(T,nu):V->L by summing nu_y(W_w(T_y phi)) over Y.
hypotheses: V is an L-module; the finite component index is actual data, not an infinite unproved summation.
proofSteps: Compose the three existing linear maps for each y and take their finite sum.
The resulting carrier is Module.Dual L V. No continuity or identification of V with arithmetic functions is added by definition.
acceptance: This is an algebraic helper for Definition 9.5, not the construction of its raw cohomological evaluations.

uses.how: Separate summation and representative cancellation from constructing cycles, coefficient local systems and integration.

api.name: finiteEvaluation_apply
api.statement: Evaluation at phi is the finite sum in the definition; node finite-evaluation-apply.

api.name: finiteEvaluation_reindex
api.statement: Transporting both arrays along a bijection of finite index types leaves the functional unchanged; node finite-evaluation-reindex.

api.name: finiteEvaluation_representative
api.statement: Matching chart and contragredient changes in every component leave the sum unchanged; node finite-evaluation-representative.

tests.name: finite_empty
tests.statement: An empty component type gives the zero linear functional.

tests.name: finite_single
tests.statement: One component gives the composition nu composed with W_w composed with T, as existing LinearMaps.

tests.name: finite_two_components
tests.statement: Over Q with G the trivial group, two identity pullbacks and evaluation functionals scaled by 2 and -3 give value -7 on input 7.

sources.match: Finite-linear-algebra core of the source's sum, with analytic and arithmetic instantiation explicitly outside the helper.

nodes.title: Evaluation of the finite component sum
proofSteps: Apply the finite sum of linear maps to phi and reduce composition.
acceptance: No component or multiplicity is discarded.

sources.match: Evaluation API for the finite sum.

nodes.title: Reindexing finite component evaluations
nodes.statement: For a bijection e:Y'->Y, Eval(T composed with e,nu composed with e)=Eval(T,nu).
hypotheses: Y,Y' finite types and e an equivalence; both arrays are transported together.
proofSteps: Apply linear-map extensionality, then reindex the finite sum by e.
acceptance: Reordering representatives is separate from changing the representative within a ray class.

sources.match: Derived finite-sum API used before nontrivial representative changes.

nodes.title: Representative independence of a compatible evaluation system
nodes.statement: Suppose T'_y(phi)(z)=T_y(phi)(u_y z) and nu'_y(h)=nu_y(z |-> w(u_y^-1)h(u_y z)) for every y,phi,z,h. Then Eval(T',nu')=Eval(T,nu).
hypotheses: Finite-evaluation hypotheses, with one u_y in G per component. The transformations must be proved for the actual arithmetic data before instantiation.
proofSteps: For each phi expand both finite sums.
Apply rechart-pairing to each summand and conclude by extensionality.
acceptance: Does not assume independence as a field of an EvaluationSystem structure; the hypotheses concern the separately checkable two input transformations.

sources.match: Corrected algebraic implication, not a claim that every required local-system map has been constructed.

nodes.title: Eigenvalue of a simultaneous refinement
nodes.statement: For a finite type P, alpha:P->L^times and n:P->N, define alpha_n=product_q alpha(q)^n(q) as a unit of L.
hypotheses: Finite P and nonzero eigenvalues represented as units. No ordering of the places is fixed.
proofSteps: Use the existing commutative group of units and its finite product operation.
acceptance: The exponent belongs to each individual prime; replacing the product by a chosen single eigenvalue fails the two-prime test.

uses.how: Supply a genuine invertible scalar for simultaneous conductor normalization.

api.name: refinementEigenvalue_step
api.statement: Increasing n(q) by one multiplies alpha_n by alpha(q); node refinement-eigenvalue-step.

tests.name: eigenvalue_empty
tests.statement: For empty P the product is the unit one.

tests.name: eigenvalue_two_primes
tests.statement: Over Q with eigenvalues 2,3 and exponents 2,1, the scalar is 12.

tests.name: eigenvalue_zero_rejected
tests.statement: There is no unit of Q whose underlying scalar is zero; a zero eigenvalue cannot be passed to this normalization.

sources.match: The scalar product in the source, with the needed invertibility hypothesis explicit.

nodes.title: Zero refinement exponent
hypotheses: Hypotheses of refinement-eigenvalue; this algebraic identity does not admit the zero modulus exponent to an arithmetic norm relation.
proofSteps: Every factor has exponent zero; the finite product of units one is one.
acceptance: Keep the distinction between the algebraically defined value and admissible arithmetic levels.

sources.locator: Product defining the eigenvalue in Theorem 9.10, p.34
sources.match: Derived algebraic API, without relaxing the source's positive level condition.

nodes.title: Adding refinement exponents
nodes.statement: alpha_(n+m)=alpha_n alpha_m, with pointwise addition of exponent vectors.
proofSteps: Expand powers of sums of natural-number exponents and distribute a finite product over multiplication in L^times.
acceptance: The proof handles an empty place set without a separate chosen prime.

sources.locator: Product defining the eigenvalue in Theorem 9.10, p.34
sources.match: Explicit multiplicativity used to compare non-linearly-ordered conductors.

nodes.title: One-prime refinement eigenvalue
nodes.statement: For the exponent vector delta_q that is one at q and zero elsewhere, alpha_(n+delta_q)=alpha(q) alpha_n.
hypotheses: Hypotheses of refinement-eigenvalue; decidable equality on the finite place type.
proofSteps: Split the exponent sum using refinement-eigenvalue-add. Only the q-factor survives in alpha_(delta_q).
acceptance: Changing q changes the scalar to the corresponding eigenvalue.

sources.match: The scalar identity matching the one-prime norm relation.

nodes.title: Normalized evaluation at a conductor
nodes.statement: For an L-module M and a family mu:(P->N)->M, define N_mu(n)=alpha_n^-1 acting on mu(n).
hypotheses: The refinement eigenvalues are units. The family is raw data; no distribution relation is packaged as an assumed theorem of a structure.
proofSteps: Coerce the inverse unit alpha_n^-1 to L and use the existing scalar action on M.
acceptance: This constructs the normalization, not mu or a p-adic L-function.

uses.how: Turn separately proved one-prime eigenrelations into conductor independence while retaining periods, eigenclass and uniformizers.

api.name: normalisedEvaluation_apply
api.statement: N_mu(n)=alpha_n^-1 acting on mu(n); node normalised-evaluation-apply.

api.name: normalisedEvaluation_step
api.statement: A one-prime relation mu(n+delta_q)=alpha(q)mu(n) implies N_mu(n+delta_q)=N_mu(n); node normalised-evaluation-step.

api.name: normalisedEvaluation_commonLevel
api.statement: All valid one-prime relations imply equality at any two componentwise positive levels; node normalised-evaluation-common-level.

tests.name: normalise_one_prime
tests.statement: Over Q with one eigenvalue 2 and mu(n)=7 times 2^n, normalization gives 7 at n=3.

tests.name: normalise_two_incomparable
tests.statement: For eigenvalues 2,3 and mu(n)=5 times 2^n0 times 3^n1, the incomparable levels (1,2) and (2,1) both normalize to 5.

tests.name: normalise_excluded_zero_level
tests.statement: For one eigenvalue 2, mu(0)=3 and mu(n)=2^n for n>=1, all positive-level norm relations hold but N_mu(0)=3 differs from N_mu(1)=1.

sources.locator: Theorem 9.10 and the hypothesis at the start of Section 9.4, pp.33-34
sources.match: Makes the normalization operation separate from its compatibility theorem and retains the all-primes-divide condition.

nodes.title: Normalized evaluation formula
proofSteps: Expose the scalar-action definition as a rewrite lemma.
acceptance: Use the inverse eigenvalue product, not the product itself.

nodes.title: Normalization cancels one prime eigenrelation
nodes.statement: If mu(n+delta_q)=alpha(q) acting on mu(n), then N_mu(n+delta_q)=N_mu(n).
hypotheses: Hypotheses of normalised-evaluation; the specific one-prime relation is explicitly assumed and must be supplied by the arithmetic trace calculation.
proofSteps: Substitute the eigenrelation and the one-prime formula for alpha_(n+delta_q).
Associativity of scalar multiplication and invertibility of alpha(q) cancel the extra factor.
acceptance: A total inverse on L with a zero eigenvalue would not justify cancellation.

sources.match: Algebraic cancellation after the genuine one-prime distribution relation has been proved.

nodes.title: Conductor independence on all positive levels
nodes.statement: Assume mu(n+delta_q)=alpha(q)mu(n) for every q and every n with n(r)>=1 for all r. Then N_mu(n)=N_mu(m) for all componentwise positive n,m.
hypotheses: Hypotheses of normalised-evaluation; finite P, with no assumption that n and m are comparable.
proofSteps: For n<=h, induct on the finite sum of coordinate differences. If it is positive choose a deficient coordinate q; incrementing it preserves positivity and strictly decreases the sum. Apply normalised-evaluation-step at each increment.
Take h(q)=max(n(q),m(q)) and compare each level with h. The empty place type has a unique exponent vector and is immediate.
acceptance: The conclusion does not include levels with a missing p-prime and does not remove the fixed uniformizer, eigenclass, period or refinement choices.

sources.match: Supplies the finite directed-level argument explicitly; arithmetic norm relations are not proved by this lemma.

sourceIssues.locator: arXiv v3, Definitions 6.3 and 6.6 and Lemma 6.7, pp.21-22; parsed text
sourceIssues.correction: Require an actual strict radius-improvement condition on the semigroup element, sufficient for the Hecke operators used. Continuity of all semigroup actions does not imply this form of compactness.
sourceIssues.reason: The identity matrix belongs to the displayed semigroup, so the statement includes the identity on the infinite-dimensional locally analytic distribution space. For F=Q, weight zero, let nu_m extract the m-th power-series coefficient at zero. Its norm on the radius-zero analytic dual is 1 and on the radius-one dual is |p|^-m. A continuous factorization of the identity from the former to the latter, required by Definition 6.6, would impose a uniform bound on |p|^-m, impossible. This checks the assertion as parsed, not the cited Urban result or the journal wording.

sourceIssues.locator: arXiv v3, Lemma 8.1(iii), p.24; parsed text
sourceIssues.correction: Require a bounded absorbing O_L-lattice stable under each of the specified U_i, rather than an arbitrary O_L-submodule. The stability should concern O_L[U_i], not all scalar multiples in L[U_i]. Then rescale a nonzero eigenvector into the lattice and use the unbounded orbit of a negative-slope eigenvalue.
sourceIssues.reason: As parsed, the norm condition is vacuous and the zero submodule satisfies the stability hypothesis. Take M=L, one operator U=p^-1 times identity and the zero submodule: the nonzero space has slope -1, contradicting the stated vanishing. A bounded absorbing lattice excludes this example and supplies both steps missing in the printed proof.
